info.name: OpenAgriNet Registry
info.description:
The Sunbird RC registry behind the stack: the seven participants and the four capability bindings that tell the provider adapter what each upstream answers. Separate from OpenAgriNet.api-collection.json, which is adapter-facing and writes to nothing.

Everything here mirrors quick-start/bin/setup.py -- the same entities, the same payloads, the same order -- so this collection is what you reach for when a row has to be inspected or repaired after the seed. Each request names the function it came from.

THE REGISTRY IS LOOPBACK-ONLY. No published port beyond 127.0.0.1 and no proxy host in front of it, by design: nothing outside the stack can reach it. Against a remote deployment, tunnel both ports first --

    ssh -L 8081:localhost:8081 -L 8080:localhost:8080 <host>

Import OpenAgriNet.local-environment.json alongside this and select it, or every {{...}} resolves to nothing.

WRITES HERE ARE MOSTLY PERMANENT. A participant's delete is soft and keeps the unique index, so an id can never be reused: think before you POST one. A ProviderSchema row is the exception -- it does take a PUT, which is what the last request is for. Read with /search freely; the answer is {totalCount, data} rather than a bare array.

item.name: 1. Auth
item.description: One request, and everything that writes needs what it returns. Search does not: bin/setup.py sends no Authorization header on any /search call, and that is what wait_for_registry() polls with.

request.description: token(), setup.py:204. The two X-Forwarded headers are not optional -- drop either and the response is 200 with an empty body, which reads as a Postman parse error rather than an auth problem.

exec: // An empty body here means the X-Forwarded headers did not reach
// Keycloak, not that the credentials are wrong.
if (!t) throw new Error('no access_token in the response');

item.name: 2. Participants
item.description:
Seven rows once bin/setup.py has run: three adapter nodes and four upstreams.

BOTH CREATES CHECK BEFORE WRITING, the way ensure_participant() does in setup.py: a pre-request script searches for the id and skips the write when it is already there, so a run against a seeded stack reads as skipped rather than failed.

TWO GUARDS SIT UNDER THAT ANYWAY. A second row for an id that exists is refused by a unique index -- public_V_Participant_participantId_sqlgIdx, by name, in the errmsg -- and the node create is refused on its key pattern while consumer-participant-key is empty. The script only stops you seeing errors that say nothing new; remove it and nothing becomes possible that was not before.

WHAT IS NOT RECOVERABLE IS THE FIRST WRITE. Delete is soft and leaves that index in place, so a participantId is never reusable: a row seeded with a wrong baseUrl or a stale public key is permanent, and the only fix is a new id in .env plus a re-run.

request.description: search(), setup.py:256. No bearer needed. The answer is {totalCount, data} rather than a bare array -- read .data.

exec: // At least seven, not exactly seven. setup.py seeds that many,
// and anything above it is somebody having registered a
// participant -- which is the point of the request below, not a
// fault. An exact count turns every legitimate addition red.
pm.test('the seven setup.py seeds are all there', () => {

request.description: The osid lookup. Change the id in the body to look up any of the seven; the osid it saves is what an Authorization header names a key by.

exec: pm.test('one row, and its osid saved', () => {
if (!rows.length) throw new Error('no such participant');

request.description:
node(), setup.py:289. One level, no {"Participant": {...}} wrapper -- a wrapper comes back as "extraneous key [...] is not permitted".

consumer-participant-key IS EMPTY IN BOTH SHIPPED ENVIRONMENTS. Paste in consumer.signingPublic from quick-start/keys/keys.json, which setup.py generates -- the signing half, not the encryption one, and not the private half of either.

Sending it empty is refused rather than stored: the schema pins keys[].key to ^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}= -- a 32-byte ed25519 public key as bare base64. That pattern is also why setup.py strips any "base64:" prefix before comparing: a label left on fails the pattern here, and fails every verification later with a decode error pointing nowhere near the registry.

exec: console.log('consumer-participant-key is empty, so this write would be'
+ ' refused on the key pattern. Fill it from quick-start/keys/'
+ 'keys.json -- the consumer.signingPublic value -- to run this.');
// 200 with params.status ERROR is the normal answer for a row
// that already exists -- setup.py searches first for that reason.

request.description:
upstream(), setup.py:308. No role, no keys, no credential. Both role and keys are permitted by the schema but neither is read -- a signature is checked against the node identity that signed it.

Against a seeded registry the pre-request script finds the row and skips the write, logging 'mausamgram: already present'. Without it the answer is HTTP 500, status UNSUCCESSFUL, and a duplicate-key errmsg naming public_V_Participant_participantId_sqlgIdx. Note the 500: Sunbird RC reports a refused write as a server error, not a 409, so an HTTP-status assertion here would be wrong. That is why the test reports instead of asserting.

item.name: 3. Capability Bindings
item.description:
The ProviderSchema entity: what each upstream answers, and where the adapter fetches the mapping that shapes it.

THE BINDING KEY IS <participantId>|<capabilityCode>. The provider adapter builds it from the incoming payload and matches it against this row, so a mismatch is a 404 -- NET_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND or "no active record".

request.description: Four rows after a seed. The mapping URL each one publishes is what the deployed stack actually fetches, so this is the request that tells you which branch is live.

exec: // At least four, for the same reason as the participant list:
// four is what setup.py seeds, not a ceiling.
pm.test('the four setup.py seeds are all there', () => {

request.description: The lookup the update needs: it saves both the row's osid and its nested action's. Run it again after an update to confirm the mapping URL really moved -- see the note on the PUT.

exec: if (!rows.length) throw new Error('no binding with that key');
// Nested objects are entities here and carry their own osid.

request.description:
ensure_binding(), setup.py:321. method is the provider's contract, not a network convention: Mausamgram and Agmarknet answer a GET whose query the mapping builds, while Vistaar and POCRA take a POST. The adapter reads it from this row, so nothing about it is compiled in -- change GET to POST here for those two.

bindingKey carries a unique index of its own, public_V_ProviderSchema_bindingKey_sqlgIdx, and the pre-request script checks for the key before writing, so this is safe to re-run twice over and CANNOT produce a second row for a key that already exists. To change an existing binding, use the PUT below rather than trying to re-create it.

RUN "Find one provider binding" FIRST -- it sets binding-osid.

What this is for: the four mapping URLs moved from the quick-start-setup branch to release-0.0.1, but editing .env only changes what the NEXT setup.py run seeds. Rows already in the registry keep the old URL, and that is the URL the provider adapter fetches.

THIS WORKS, against setup.py's docstrings. They assert three times that the registry cannot update a record; that is true of a participantId, whose delete is soft and whose unique index survives it, but not of a ProviderSchema row. Measured on Sunbird RC v2.0.0: HTTP 200, params.status SUCCESSFUL, and the mapping URL moved.

IT REPLACES THE RECORD RATHER THAN EDITING IT. The parent osid holds, but actions[] carries nested entities and each one comes back with a FRESH osid -- the old action is detached, not amended. So send the whole record: a field left out of this body is a field dropped from the row. Read the current row first and change only what you mean to, rather than rebuilding the body from .env, or a hand-typed method or timeoutMs quietly becomes the new truth.

Re-run "Find one provider binding" afterwards and read actions[0].mappings. A 200 alone does not tell you the nested action moved with it.

exec: // Deliberately not a plain status assertion: the point of this
// request is to find out which of these the registry does.
`HTTP ${code}: this registry has no update. The row cannot be ` +
`edited in place -- replace it, re-seed, or patch registry-db.`);
console.log('Now re-run "Find one provider binding" and check actions[0].mappings.');

item.name: 4. Capability Schemas
item.description:
The SchemaRegistry entity: what a capabilityCode MEANS, as opposed to who serves it. One row per capability, pointing at the schema pack in OpenAgriNet/network-specs that defines its attributes.

SEEDED, AS OF THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THIS FOLDER. bin/setup.py now writes all four rows, so a fresh stack comes up with them and every request here reads or re-reads rather than filling a gap. It did not before: the entity was mounted, uniquely indexed and empty, with nothing in the quick-start able to put a row in it.

ONE VARIABLE DRIVES THE WHOLE FOLDER. Set capability-code and every request follows, the two writes included -- schemaUrl and the display name are derived from it by a pre-request script, the same way setup.py's schema_url() derives them, because a capability code already contains its pack's directory name. Nothing in a request body needs editing to work on a different capability, and the code cannot end up naming a different pack than the URL does.

THE ENTITY IS REAL, not a leftover: config/registry/schemas/SchemaRegistry.json is mounted at /home/sunbirdrc/config/public/_schemas alongside Participant and ProviderSchema. Schemas are read at startup, so editing one needs sunbird-registry-service restarted before the registry honours it.

schemaUrl IS PATTERN-CHECKED, and narrowly: a raw.githubusercontent URL under OpenAgriNet/network-specs, with a schema/<Capability>/v<major>.<minor>/<name>.yaml path. version is checked against ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ and capabilityCode against ^openagrinet:[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$, so a typo in any of the three is refused rather than stored.

request.description: Expect totalCount 0 unless someone has posted a row by hand -- see the folder description.

exec: // Not an assertion on the count at all. setup.py seeds four, and
// network-specs carries eight packs, so a fifth or a sixth is
// somebody extending the deployment rather than breaking it.
: 'none registered -- setup.py does not seed this entity');

console.log('not registered -- run "Register a capability schema" first');

request.description:
SKIPPED AGAINST A SEEDED STACK, like the other three creates in this collection -- setup.py writes all four schema rows now, so the pre-request script finds the row and does not write. It is the request to reach for when adding a capability setup.py does not know about; the eight packs in network-specs outnumber the four capabilities this deployment serves. Point capability-code at one of the other four and it writes for real.

schema-pack-ref IS main, AND main DOES NOT SERVE THIS PATH YET -- it is a 404 today; only the schema-packs-v0.1 branch answers 200. The registry only pattern-checks the URL's shape and never fetches it, so the row stores either way: main is the value that becomes correct when the schema packs merge, and pointing at the branch instead would resolve now but break on delete. Change this one variable to switch.

capabilityCode is uniquely indexed, so a second row for the same capability is refused; correcting a URL means the PUT below, not a re-create.

exec: throw new Error(`capability-code must be <prefix>:<Pack>, got '${code}'`);
// WeatherObservation -> Weather Observation, which is what the pack's own
// info.title says once its 'OpenAgriNet -' and 'Attributes' are stripped.
// What the pre-request script derived, so a surprise is
// visible here rather than in the stored row.

request.description:
RUN "Find one capability by code" FIRST -- it sets capability-osid. Without it the URL ends in a bare slash and the answer is 405, which is not the real behaviour below.

THIS FAILS TODAY, AND NOT BECAUSE OF THE BODY. It answers UNSUCCESSFUL with 'extraneous key [osid] is not permitted' and the same for osOwner, osCreatedAt, osUpdatedAt, osCreatedBy, osUpdatedBy. On an update the registry merges the STORED record into the body and re-validates the result, so those six system fields arrive on their own and are then rejected.

THE CAUSE IS ONE FLAG. SchemaRegistry.json sets additionalProperties false; Participant.json and ProviderSchema.json both set it true, which is why PUT works on those two and not this one. Set it true and restart sunbird-registry-service -- schemas are read at startup -- and this request starts working.

UNTIL THEN A schemaUrl IS FIXED FOR THE ROW'S LIFETIME, which matters because moving refs is exactly what this field is for. Delete is soft and the unique index on capabilityCode survives it, so a wrong URL cannot be corrected by re-creating the row either.

PUT REPLACES THE RECORD once it does work, so all five required fields belong in this body -- one left out is one dropped from the row.
